roleTitle: Microsoft Senior Customer Success Account Manager

job.location: United States; up to 50% work from home; specific base location not stated in the supplied posting
job.rawJd: Microsoft is hiring Senior Customer Success Account Managers across enterprise, regulated, and partner services organizations in the United States. The CSAM is the delivery leader in the account team and a strategic customer partner responsible for executing Customer Success Contracts, orchestrating cross-functional programs, and helping customers realize business outcomes from Microsoft Cloud solutions and support. Responsibilities include building customer, partner, and internal stakeholder relationships; leading business-value conversations with technical, business, and executive stakeholders; gathering business and IT objectives; contributing to customer success and account plans; aligning Azure, Modern Work, Dynamics, and other Microsoft capabilities to customer priorities; coordinating specialists for complex and cross-cloud scenarios; leading program planning, customer-facing reviews, prioritization, escalation communication, and delivery-resource orchestration; identifying and mitigating blockers to consumption; tracking consumption milestones; driving adoption and usage; and identifying added value that supports retention and reduces churn. Minimum qualifications are a master's degree in a related field plus 3 years of customer success, solution delivery, practice management, customer-facing consulting, or portfolio management experience, or a bachelor's degree plus 4 years, or equivalent experience. The role is not eligible for visa sponsorship and requires U.S. work authorization that does not now or in the future require sponsorship. Preferred qualifications include 10-12+ years of relevant experience depending on degree, 5+ years in the customer industry, Microsoft or competitor cloud certification, ITIL or equivalent service-management certification, PMI or equivalent project-management certification, and Prosci or equivalent change-management certification. The role can work up to 50% from home, with travel varying by assignment. The posted base-pay range is $106,400-$203,600 across the U.S., with a separate range for the San Francisco Bay Area and New York City.
